domainMaps.title: Domain Map: Usable App Authentication & App-Owned Authorization
domainMaps.content:
# Usable App Authentication & App-Owned Authorization Domain Map

This map routes authentication and authorization work for applications registered through Usable Apps or Marketplace. It covers interactive web, SPA, mobile, desktop, and service-to-service clients by loading client-specific references only when applicable.

## Platform and application boundary

- Usable owns OIDC identity, Marketplace client registration, configured application eligibility, and Usable API scopes.
- Each application explicitly decides whether it needs app-owned roles or capabilities; platform eligibility never silently creates product privilege.
- OAuth client type determines secret and session handling.
- The public API repeats authentication, eligibility, and authorization checks and fails closed.
- Flowcore owns application-domain mutation history where the application adopts Flowcore; projections remain read models.
- Operational session/token storage is infrastructure state and cannot become an authorization command path.

## Applicability boundary

The shared memory-mesh and installed-group rules apply to Usable Marketplace applications using Usable identity. Standalone Flowcore SaaS/customer products that are not Marketplace applications remain governed by their own authentication domain and realm standard.

## Execution Rules

1. Fetch every required reference before planning.
2. Evaluate every conditional reference against application type, access-control policy, scopes, session model, authorization model, and event architecture.
3. Prefer newer released and approved sources when an older recipe or draft conflicts.
4. Produce a compliance receipt addressing USABLE-AUTH-C1 through USABLE-AUTH-C11 before implementation.
5. If Flowcore mutations are in scope, load the Flowcore Pathways Domain Map and apply its required references and constraints too.
6. Resolve current application configuration and full UUIDs at runtime; never reuse example clients, scopes, groups, redirects, or secrets from a source fragment.

## Scope exclusions

This map does not define an application's product-specific roles, membership limits, tenants, organizations, onboarding policy, or feature permissions. Those belong in that application's accepted decisions and specifications.

frontmatter.description: General-purpose Usable Apps domain for Marketplace/OIDC identity, configured installation or access-policy eligibility, app-owned authorization, client-specific credential custody, claim and scope validation, provisioning and revocation, optional bootstrap, and Flowcore event boundaries.

required.summary: Released public Usable documentation for application and Marketplace surfaces, authorization expectations, secret handling, and current interface boundaries.
Cross-cutting approved rule that Usable Marketplace apps use the shared memory-mesh realm and therefore require client binding and app-side eligibility enforcement.
Released Marketplace OAuth trust classification: SPA, mobile, and desktop are public and secretless; confidential secret operations require type, stored, and live Keycloak agreement.
Verified reusable boundary for Usable identity and eligibility, app-owned capabilities, fail-closed validation, durable sessions, revocation, and optional event-sourced bootstrap.
Adversarially verified implementation evidence for JWT type checks, installed-group gating, app-owned roles, token custody, concurrency, and durable bootstrap.

conditional.condition: application access policy uses installation or invitation eligibility
conditional.summary: Canonical Marketplace installed-group claim and invite-only provisioning/revocation flow with event-driven installation records.

conditional.condition: application calls Usable APIs with Marketplace bearer tokens or declares Usable API permissions
conditional.summary: Canonical dotted Usable permission scopes, exact scope enforcement, registered-client trust, and no fallback for unknown Marketplace clients.

conditional.condition: confidential web application uses refresh_token or offline_access through a BFF
conditional.summary: Verified encrypted server-side provider-token custody, opaque browser session references, refresh handling, and federated logout.

conditional.condition: desktop Marketplace OAuth client is in scope
conditional.summary: Released exact-loopback Authorization Code plus PKCE S256 desktop client with no secret and fail-closed configuration validation.

conditional.condition: application persists or exchanges stable Usable user identity across services
conditional.summary: Accepted decision for using the signed full Usable user UUID claim instead of mutable email or lookup tables.

conditional.condition: application-owned authorization, provisioning, revocation, or bootstrap mutations use Flowcore
conditional.summary: Governing Flowcore Pathways domain: domain writes are events, projections are read models, and no direct-database fallback exists.

conditional.condition: scaffolding a full internal Usable Marketplace application
conditional.summary: End-to-end implementation standard for internal Usable applications, including client registration, sessions, authorization, event paths, verification, and delivery.

constraints.text: A Usable Marketplace application MUST follow the Usable Application standard and use its Marketplace-provisioned client in the shared memory-mesh realm unless newer authoritative Usable documentation explicitly changes that contract. Signature and issuer validation alone are insufficient in the shared realm; bearer tokens MUST be bound to the exact registered client.
constraints.failure_mode: A dedicated-realm assumption or issuer-only validation accepts tokens minted for another Usable application.

constraints.text: Every protected request MUST validate the applicable chain before business logic: pinned-issuer JWKS signature, explicitly allowed algorithm, issuer, expiry and nbf, exact registered-client binding through azp, access-token type when the issuer supplies one, configured application eligibility, then every required application capability and/or Usable API scope.
constraints.failure_mode: Omitted or reordered checks accept ID tokens, foreign-client tokens, ineligible users, or callers missing the operation permission.

constraints.text: The application MUST enforce its current configured access-control policy and MUST fail closed when required eligibility evidence is missing, malformed, stale, or unavailable. When installation or invitation is the eligibility mechanism, require the exact installed group derived from the full application UUID; NEVER silently default an unreadable policy or groups claim to public access.
constraints.failure_mode: A mapper outage, missing claim, or policy parsing error admits the whole Usable user population.

constraints.text: Usable identity, Marketplace eligibility, workspace eligibility, and application authorization are separate boundaries. When the application owns roles or capabilities, NEVER infer them from Usable workspace roles, Marketplace administration, or installation alone. Handlers MUST declare and enforce application capabilities at the API; UI checks are advisory only.
constraints.failure_mode: An external platform role silently becomes product privilege, or hidden UI controls remain callable through the API.

constraints.text: User-linked application state MUST use the stable full Usable user UUID from a verified signed claim, never email or a shortened UUID. Persist only identity data required by the application and do not copy display names or email into access events or authorization projections unless a separately approved requirement needs it.
constraints.failure_mode: Mutable or truncated identifiers break linking and revocation; unnecessary PII expands replay and breach exposure.

constraints.text: Marketplace clients calling Usable APIs MUST request only the registered scopes they need and APIs MUST enforce exact canonical permission names from the token. A missing required scope is a denial, and an unknown or inactive Marketplace client MUST NOT fall back to cookie, PAT, or another authentication path.
constraints.failure_mode: Over-broad tokens or fallback authentication bypass the permission and registered-client boundary.

constraints.text: OAuth client security MUST be derived server-side from application type. SPA, mobile, and desktop clients are public and secretless; they MUST use Authorization Code with PKCE where supported and MUST never ship or reveal a client secret. Confidential web and service-to-service secret operations require agreement between type-derived classification, stored classification, and live Keycloak state, and verification failure MUST fail closed.
constraints.failure_mode: An extractable public-client secret is treated as protection, or stale database metadata reveals or rotates credentials for the wrong client.

constraints.text: Credential and session custody MUST match the client class. A confidential browser application using a BFF MUST keep provider access, refresh, and ID tokens encrypted server-side and give the browser only an HTTP-only session with an opaque reference; refresh MUST be serialized, rejected refresh MUST require reauthentication, logout MUST destroy local and provider sessions, and internal token endpoints MUST not be publicly ingressed. Public clients MUST use PKCE and platform-appropriate secure token storage without a client secret.
constraints.failure_mode: Provider credentials leak to browser code or public ingress, refresh rotation races corrupt sessions, or logout leaves reusable credentials active.

constraints.text: Platform eligibility and application-owned authorization MUST remain independently revocable. A caller that no longer satisfies the current access policy MUST be denied even if an application assignment remains, and an application-revoked caller MUST be denied even if Marketplace eligibility remains. Revocation and provisioning operations MUST be idempotent and API enforcement MUST not trust stale UI or cache state after verification failure.
constraints.failure_mode: Stale state on either side preserves access after uninstall, invitation withdrawal, workspace removal, role revocation, or upstream failure.

constraints.text: When application-owned authorization, provisioning, revocation, or bootstrap is a Flowcore domain mutation, it MUST be emitted as a Flowcore event and projected into read models. NEVER write authorization projections directly and NEVER add a direct-database fallback when the event path is unavailable. Operational auth-session storage may be transactional infrastructure state but MUST NOT mutate application authorization.
constraints.failure_mode: A session table or emergency SQL path becomes an unaudited authorization command path and breaks event replay.

constraints.text: If an application requires initial privileged bootstrap, it MUST use an explicit, durable, replay-safe singleton claim after all applicable identity and eligibility checks. NEVER infer bootstrap from an empty role count, NEVER allow concurrent claims to create multiple initial assignments, and NEVER expose an application shortcut that reactivates a consumed bootstrap.
constraints.failure_mode: Concurrent first logins, projection loss, or configuration changes remint initial privilege.

domainMaps.summary: General-purpose Domain Map for Usable Apps authentication and app-owned authorization: Marketplace/OIDC identity, access-policy eligibility, client binding, scopes, credential custody, provisioning/revocation, optional bootstrap, and Flowcore event boundaries.

domainMaps.title: Domain Map: Flowcore Pathways
domainMaps.content:
# Flowcore Pathways Domain Map

This fragment is a machine-readable routing layer for context re-inflation. Autonomous agents (like Symphony or Hermes) must fetch the referenced fragments before planning tasks in this domain.

## Mandatory Collections

When working in this domain, agents should be aware of the following collections:
- **[Flowcore Data Pathways](https://usable.dev/dashboard/workspaces/60c10ca2-4115-4c1a-b6d7-04ac39fd3938/fragments?collection=bf9a6ae6-bf00-484d-a7f5-c471ada5e736)** — Required for understanding and working with *Managed Pathways*.
- **[@flowcore/pathways Library](https://usable.dev/dashboard/workspaces/60c10ca2-4115-4c1a-b6d7-04ac39fd3938/fragments?collection=b232ad64-ac3e-42ff-811a-8513eab5e484)** — Required for working with both *Managed* and *Virtual Pathways*.

> **Note:** The Virtual Pathway with Auto-Provisioning is the default and preferred approach.

## Execution Rules

1. **Pre-flight Check:** Before writing an implementation plan, the agent must fetch the `doctrine` fragments (`c748f425-dd0e-47a4-9eb5-37008fe7a928` and `79a08d39-e7b5-44ec-a3c0-262f292a1b22`).
2. **Harness Selection:** The agent must evaluate the `conditional` fragments and fetch the ones matching the current stack and feature requirements.
3. **Artifact Generation:** The agent must produce a `<compliance_receipt>` addressing constraints `PATHWAYS-C1` through `PATHWAYS-C5` before generating code.

frontmatter.description: Flowcore's mandatory event-driven architecture. The Virtual Pathway with Auto-Provisioning is the default approach. All state mutations must occur via event emission. Direct database writes from API handlers are strictly prohibited.

required.summary: Core rules — Event Sourcing, CQRS, no direct DB writes, YAML vs TypeScript boundaries
Virtual Pathways Auto-Provisioning — The default pattern, describing declarative registration and auto-provisioning without flowcore.yaml.

conditional.summary: Pathways Integration Pattern — PathwaysBuilder, PathwayRouter, type-safe handlers

conditional.condition: feature requires request-response or synchronous-like feedback
conditional.summary: Request-Response Pattern — emit event, delay, poll database for projection result

constraints.text: NEVER write to the database directly from an API handler or service. All writes MUST be emitted as events via pathways.write().
constraints.failure_mode: Direct DB write = architecture defect, bypasses event log and audit trail

constraints.text: NEVER parse event payloads manually in transformers. Use FlowcoreEvent<z.infer<typeof Schema>> in the function signature.
constraints.failure_mode: Manual parsing = type safety defect, reinventing built-in validation

constraints.text: Choose the write completion mode based on where the handler runs. (1) Handler registered in this service (local pump or cluster): await pathways.write(). The promise resolves on handler completion. Read the projection and return the real resource. Do not pass fireAndForget. (2) Handler is remote, the work is long-running, or the runtime is serverless/stateless: pass fireAndForget: true, return { id, status: 'processing' }, and let the client poll the projection. (3) Write-only pathways (register({ writable: true, subscribe: false })): no local handler exists, so fireAndForget: true is correct. Document which mode each pathway-driven feature uses.
constraints.failure_mode: Blanket fire-and-forget on local CRUD returns 2xx while the handler throws and the projection stays empty — silent data loss with no error surface. Blanket awaiting on a remote, long-running, or serverless path blocks the request until pathwayTimeoutMs (default 10000 ms) and breaks async decoupling.

constraints.text: NEVER modify event history. Events are append-only immutable facts.
constraints.failure_mode: Updating past events = audit trail destruction, invalidates event sourcing

constraints.text: Virtual Pathways with auto-provisioning is the default. NEVER require manual flowcore.yaml creation unless explicitly building a legacy managed pathway.
constraints.failure_mode: Manual flowcore.yaml = deprecated approach, breaks auto-provisioning flow

domainMaps.summary: Knowledge Domain Map for Flowcore Pathways & Event-Driven Architecture, containing required doctrine, conditional patterns, and incompressible constraints for context re-inflation.

domainMaps.title: Domain Map: Drizzle ORM & PostgreSQL
domainMaps.content:
# Drizzle ORM & PostgreSQL Domain Map

This fragment is a machine-readable routing layer for context re-inflation. Autonomous agents (like Symphony or Hermes) must fetch the referenced fragments before planning tasks in this domain.

## Execution Rules

1. **Pre-flight Check:** Before writing a database schema or query plan, the agent must fetch the `doctrine` fragments (`3312059c-dae7-49ea-84bc-ac192358c35e`, `a88e2104-81e2-4bc1-8b4f-db545f857bfa`, and `db33693c-6681-4b3e-82de-b5487ef62a54`).
2. **Harness Selection:** The agent must evaluate the `conditional` fragments and fetch the ones matching the current data complexity.
3. **Artifact Generation:** The agent must produce a `<compliance_receipt>` addressing constraints `DRIZZLE-C1` through `DRIZZLE-C7` before generating schema code.

## Deployment migrations

Deploy-time schema changes use checked-in, journaled SQL migrations. Keep `drizzle-kit push` limited to local development against disposable databases. Review generated SQL before deployment and keep Pathways-owned runtime tables outside application migrations.

## Choosing a migrator

Prefer **drizzle-orm's migrator** (`drizzle-orm/postgres-js/migrator`) over the `drizzle-kit migrate` CLI for anything that runs in a container: drizzle-kit is normally a `devDependency`, so a pruned or `--production` image loses it, while `drizzle-orm` is a runtime dependency you already ship. `drizzle-kit migrate` is fine where the CLI is guaranteed present.

frontmatter.description: Flowcore's standard for PostgreSQL as a projection layer. The database is a read-model derived from events, not the source of truth. Strict rules apply regarding foreign keys, extensions, and how schema changes reach a deployed environment.

required.summary: Core rules — No Foreign Key constraints in event-sourced schemas to prevent race conditions.
PostgreSQL Extensions — Restrictions on pg_trgm, unaccent, and managed environment gotchas.
Why drizzle-kit push must never run unattended, and how to baseline an existing push-provisioned database onto journaled migrations.

conditional.condition: schema handles multi-source or complex JSON data
conditional.summary: Drizzle Schema for Multi-Source Ingestion (cursor:jsonb pattern).

conditional.condition: the project still uses db:push for LOCAL development, or generates migrations in a repo that uses @flowcore/pathways
conditional.summary: Using tablesFilter in drizzle.config.ts so pathways-owned runtime tables are never dropped or migrated.

examples.summary: service-tenant-api: Database Schema & Data Model — Full Drizzle ORM setup.

constraints.text: NEVER use Foreign Key constraints between tables in event-sourced systems. Use logical relations.
constraints.failure_mode: Foreign keys cause race conditions when events arrive out of order, breaking the projection layer.

constraints.text: PostgreSQL is a PROJECTION layer, not the source of truth. The event log is the source of truth.
constraints.failure_mode: Treating DB as source of truth leads to direct writes and audit trail destruction.

constraints.text: NEVER assume PostgreSQL extensions (like pg_trgm or unaccent) are available by default in managed environments. A migration that uses gin_trgm_ops or vector_cosine_ops MUST create its extension with CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS first.
constraints.failure_mode: Migrations fail in production due to missing superuser privileges, or fail on a fresh database with 'operator class gin_trgm_ops does not exist'.

constraints.text: Deploy-time schema changes MUST use journaled migrations (checked-in SQL in ./drizzle, applied by a migrator). `drizzle-kit push` is a LOCAL DEVELOPMENT tool and MUST NEVER run in a deploy hook, CI deploy step, or any unattended context.
constraints.failure_mode: push diffs the live database and renders an interactive prompt on destructive or ambiguous changes. With no TTY the prompt never resolves and the deploy Job hangs until the cluster kills it. `--force` does not fix this — it auto-approves every statement including DROP and TRUNCATE. Closing stdin does not fix it either; push blocks on EOF rather than aborting (measured).

constraints.text: The @flowcore/pathways library owns its runtime state tables (pathway_state, pathway_pump_state). NEVER manage them from application migrations, and NEVER let a schema diff drop them. Mirror them read-only in the ORM schema and use `tablesFilter` (e.g. ["!pathway_*"]) in drizzle.config.ts so neither `push` nor `generate` touches them.
constraints.failure_mode: A diff drops the state tables or a generated migration re-creates them, corrupting event processing pointers.

constraints.text: drizzle-kit <= 0.30 CANNOT introspect `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT`. Any schema using .nullsNotDistinct() will be re-diffed by `push` forever — it re-plans a drop+re-add on every run. Such a schema CANNOT be maintained with push once the affected tables hold rows.
constraints.failure_mode: Every deploy prompts 'You're about to add <constraint> ... Do you want to truncate <table>?' and hangs.

constraints.text: When converting an existing push-provisioned database to journaled migrations, the 0000 baseline MUST be idempotent: IF NOT EXISTS on every CREATE TABLE/INDEX, a duplicate_object guard around every CREATE TYPE, and no DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE anywhere. Only the baseline needs these guards; later generated migrations do not.
constraints.failure_mode: A non-idempotent baseline aborts on the first CREATE TABLE against the live database, or worse, is 'fixed' by someone adding a DROP.

domainMaps.summary: Knowledge Domain Map for Drizzle ORM & PostgreSQL. deploy-time schema changes MUST use journaled migrations; `drizzle-kit push` is a local-dev tool and MUST NOT run in an unattended deploy hook. Adds DRIZZLE-C6 for the drizzle-kit <=0.30 UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT introspection defect.

## Execution Rules

frontmatter.description: Flowcore's standard for Next.js frontends. Enforces strict component layering (ui -> shared -> feature), TanStack ecosystem usage, and event-driven state mutations via server actions.

required.summary: Frontend Component Architecture: The SOLID application to shadcn/ui base → token-themed ui/ → configurable shared/ → feature compositions.
Architecture & SOLID Standards: The golden path for code shape and dependency inversion.

conditional.condition: implementing forms, data fetching, or event emission
conditional.summary: SaaS Template Part 3: Next.js 16 architecture, TanStack Forms/Query, and emitEvent() server actions.
React Hook Form to TanStack Forms Migration: Concrete examples of TanStack Form implementation.

examples.summary: UI Components Standards: Concrete examples of shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS usage.

constraints.text: NEVER create a new primitive UI component if a shadcn/ui equivalent exists. If it doesn't fit, extend it — do not replace it.
constraints.failure_mode: Component duplication and design system fragmentation.

constraints.text: Frontend components MUST follow the strict layering rule: ui/ (primitives) -> shared/ (configurable compositions) -> <feature>/ (business logic). Feature components can import from shared/ and ui/, but NEVER the reverse.

constraints.text: NEVER mutate data directly from the frontend. ALL state mutations MUST be emitted as events via server actions calling emitEvent().

constraints.text: NEVER access process.env directly in components. ALWAYS use T3 Env (src/lib/env.ts) with Zod validation.

## Execution Rules

1. **Pre-flight Check:** Before writing a test plan, the agent must fetch the `doctrine` fragment (`df4cc063-8e3f-4b34-9d25-cca7a3d838d3`).
2. **Harness Selection:** The agent must evaluate the `conditional` fragments and fetch the one matching the current stack.
3. **Artifact Generation:** The agent must produce a `<compliance_receipt>` addressing constraints `BBT-C1` through `BBT-C6` before generating code.

frontmatter.description: Usable's mandatory testing approach. All tests interact only through public interfaces — HTTP, UI, CLI, events. Zero internal imports.

required.summary: Core rules — DO/DON'T table, boundary definition, zero internal imports

conditional.summary: vitest + webhook fixture pattern, DB-gated skip, CI Postgres service
Playwright + real Keycloak + webhook mock server architecture

examples.summary: Klokkan: Black-Box Test Harness & CI/CD Infrastructure
bun-webhook-service: Testing Strategy — Specific WebhookTestFixture and AuthFixture implementations
Usable E2E Harness — Playwright + Real Keycloak + Flowcore Webhook Fixture

constraints.text: NEVER import from /src in test files. Zero internal imports. Tests interact only through HTTP, UI, CLI, or events.
constraints.failure_mode: Internal import = white-box test = invalid regardless of pass/fail

constraints.text: NEVER create a custom test harness or custom webhook server. Use the existing WebhookTestFixture pattern from fragment 91361703.
constraints.failure_mode: Custom harness = reinvented wheel, breaks consistency, wastes time

constraints.text: NEVER mock pathways.write with a no-op. Mock it with deliverEvent() so the real handler + DB projection runs.
constraints.failure_mode: No-op mock = test passes but nothing was actually tested

constraints.text: Docker Compose runs ONLY Postgres/Keycloak/Arango. NEVER add a webhook-fixture sidecar container.
constraints.failure_mode: Sidecar container = wrong architecture, breaks the in-process fixture pattern

constraints.text: Playwright E2E tests MUST follow black-box principles. Capture screenshots at every meaningful step. These screenshots MUST be uploaded as CI artifacts and attached to PR descriptions as visual evidence.
constraints.failure_mode: Missing screenshots = manual QA required, breaks visual verification loop

constraints.text: NEVER write shallow 'happy path' smoke tests. Playwright E2E tests MUST cover all designed states: Happy, Empty, Error (invalid input, 403, 404, network failure), Success, and Loading.
constraints.failure_mode: Shallow tests = false confidence, UI edge cases and error states fail in production

domainMaps.summary: Knowledge Domain Map for Black-Box Testing, containing required doctrine, conditional harness patterns, worked examples, and incompressible constraints for context re-inflation.
